descriptions.description:
Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT) identifies a structural architecture governing stability across interacting human systems. A minimal dynamical formulation of this
architecture is defined by capacity 𝐶(𝑡), boundary permeability 𝐵(𝑡), and effective
load 𝐿(𝑡), together with the instability condition
𝑑𝐿/𝑑𝑡 > 𝜅(𝐶, 𝐵) (1)
This paper extends the minimal system to distributed environments in which interacting systems exchange load across permeable boundaries. The stability variables
extend to spatial fields 𝐶(𝑥, 𝑡), 𝐵(𝑥, 𝑡), and 𝐿(𝑥, 𝑡), transforming the local dynamical
system into a distributed stability field.
This field is governed by a nonlinear stability equation of the form
𝜕𝐿/𝜕𝑡 = 𝐷 ∇2𝐿 + 𝑃(ℓ(𝑥, 𝑡)) − 𝜅(𝐶(𝑥, 𝑡), 𝐵(𝑥, 𝑡))
The resulting system is governed by a nonlinear field equation capturing load propagation, dissipation, and cross-system coupling. Stability and instability arise as spatial regimes separated by a dynamically evolving boundary. This formulation establishes the field-level mechanics of stability within DHFT and provides the basis for
subsequent analysis of propagation, containment, and collapse across interacting
systems.

https://zenodo.org/records/19076116

Full DHFT Formal System Repository: https://osf.io/9psmd/

Falsifiability and Failure Conditions

DHFT is falsified only if its governing structural relations fail—specifically, if load under constraint does not produce instability or reorganization, if interpretation alone alters system behavior, if propagation fails under coupling, or if projection violates structural invariance.
DHFT does not model subjective experience (thought, emotion, perception) as variables; dimensionality refers to structural degrees of freedom in system dynamics, not experiential or psychological dimensions.

Within DHFT, Dimensional Human Physics (DHP) defines the lawful structural mechanics of load, capacity, and boundary conditions. Despite its name, “physics” refers to structural mechanics rather than material or biological processes.

DHFT is stewarded by the Somatic Rising Institute, founded by Cara Tonucci. 

Somatic Rising Institute (SRI): 
www.somaticrisinginstitute.org
